Knysna Council Crisis

By: Catherine Rice | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Once the jewel in the crown of the Garden Route, the town of Knysna has fallen into a state of complete collapse.

Unique Selling Point:
Towns across South Africa are suffering the effects of corrupt and incompetent municipal management. But, Knysna's situation is dramatically more serious than most due to its importance as a tourism hub, and the ecological significance of its estuary and lagoon, home to the endagered Knysna seahorse.

Summary:
The Knysna estuary is the most biodiverse estuary in the country. It is where the only endemic species of seahorse can be found in South Africa. Although a popular swimming and fishing spot, swimming was banned by the municipality in the Knysna lagoon for two weeks in December due to pollution from sewage spills. The town of Knysna has been experiencing a number of service delivery problems, including refuse piling up in the streets, sewage pollution and water shortages. In November last year, a decomposing body was found in one of its reservoirs. As a result, it had to be drained and disinfected, and some residents were without water for several weeks. The Knysna Local Municipality is governed by a coalition that includes the EFF, PA and PBI. It's led by the ANC. It's been plagued by governance issues since it's formation in August 2022. The rot set in long before this coalition came to power, however, but it's decline has accelerated at an alarming rate in the past year, and the town is now facing bankruptcy.

Further information:
Last year, the DA spent much of the year wrapped up in litigation against the municipality for illegal appointments. Now, the DA's provincial authorities in the Western Cape have stepped in with a list of problems in a diagnostic report that will be tabled in council in March. The municipality will have to accept the report and the proposed solutions for life in the town to change. Placing the municipality under administration would be a last resort. Described as a "coalition of corruption" by the opposition (the DA), the municipality's incompetence has become visible in all quarters of this once pristine holiday town. Infrastructure MMC Beauty Charlie has allegedly done nothing to maintain infrastructure, and the collapse is visible everywhere. The buck stops with Mayor Aubrey Tshwega. What is he doing to turn the situation around? We find out.

Script:


VO 1 There’s no denying Knysna’s beauty. In fact, from the air, the jewel of the Garden Route, a favourite among tourists, is even more impressive.

NATSOUND “Its actually amazing to see it from the air”

VO 2 Holiday homes line a lagoon protected from the sea by its two famous sandstone heads, and in the distance the sparkling Indian Ocean.

Pause

VO 3 Beside me is John Meterlerkamp, a concerned businessman from Knysna - a town he says…is in freefall.

NATSOUND: The informal settlements stretch 11 kms, township round back of hills. The township below us has been without water for two weeks. If you see those three little inlets to the left of us, behind it is the sewage works, it's not working. It's dangerous to swim in this water.

VO 4 The causes of the problems are complex: the Covid pandemic, a struggling economy, poor infrastructure maintenance and an exploding population all contributed.

VO 5 Now a town wracked by political horse-trading, Knysna’s decay is undeniable…

Pause

VO 6 Something as obvious from 1000 feet above the ground…

VO 7 … as it is below the surface of the lagoon.

VO 8: This is the natural habitat of the Knysna Seahorse. An endangered species whose very existence is intertwined with the health of the lagoon. An ecosystem as fragile as this one relies on proper management – something horribly lacking in the adjacent town. So, as odd as it sounds, this story is as much about politics and the failure of local government as it is about the survival of a Seahorse.

LINK It’s about how the wellbeing of that seahorse reflects a complex relationship between land and sea…a relationship that’s gone badly awry because of who is in charge here...

VO 9: You see, the worse things get at Knysna’s town hall, the worse they become for its residents. And both those things are bad news for the humble Seahorse.

LINK The Knysna Local Municipality is run by an ANC led coalition. Audio recordings of the first council meeting of this year shows just how dysfunctional that coalition is with the meeting ending in chaos.

NATSOUND Council meeting Time code: 00:10 “We are sitting with waste issues, water issues, in Knysna, can we deal with the business of the day”. (Time stamp January 31)

NATSOUND “This report is a very distressing read” “This municipality cannot collapse”

NATSOUND Are you running council? Are you running council? …where are you? Shut up man. Are you running council? There’s no outright winner here. The ANC mustn’t come here and think they’re in charge here. Councillors councillors. You cannot mention the ANC that we must be quiet. The ANC cannot be quiet. Just as much as they need me I need them. Can I see all the chief whips in my office please. 02:05 They can fucking go to hell. (Time stamp 31 January)

VO 10 This is an environment ripe for political sabotage and manipulation. Just eighteen months ago the coalition government, led by the Democratic Alliance, was booted out of power after several motions of no confidence were brought against its leadership. And while coalitions collapse, and new ones are formed, little is being done to run this town effectively.

VO 11 Visible signs of infrastructure collapse are everywhere - despite just over a billion rand budget, Knysna is on the brink of financial collapse.

VO 12 For Lynn Kayster, a local activist in Hornlee - an area of Knysna that has been without water for weeks, every day has become a fight for her community.

UPSOUND Lynn Kayster / Hornlee resident: We are pushed to the extreme when the frustration builds up. We are trying from our side as the community to assist this municipality and you’re just hitting on closed doors”.

NATSOUND We’re going where we need to protect our feet…Erin: From? From sewage

VO 13 Water shortages are not Lynn’s only concern. Sewage spills happen constantly .. ending up in the stream further down.

UPSOUND Lynn Kayster: You can actually see where it fills up. I don’t see anything being done, this stream speaks for itself. For me it was like they would fight for the seahorses and the fish and then that would be fixed for us too, but even that fell on deaf ears.

V O 14 So who is in charge of the Municipality? Right now, its Aubrey Tsengwa… the ANC executive mayor - who's been in power since August 2022….

VO 15 Who ironically, back in 2013 was fired by the Municipality that he now runs. At the time he worked as a law enforcement officer and was dismissed because of his alleged involvement in a violent scuffle that broke out at an ANC meeting..

UPSOUND Aubrey Tsengwa: And I was dismissed based on other things, politics during that time.

ERIN: With that on your track record do you feel that you are a fitting person to hold office of Mayor of Knysna?

UPSOUND Aubrey Tsengwa: I am fit for purpose. Yes, I’m the right person to lead the town despite these small challenges which we are facing at the municipality. I can assure you we will deal with people not prepared to do their work.

VO 16 But, the mayor’s promises ring hollow for the Hornlee community. Many people here are unemployed, and their situation has been deteriorating for years.

VOX: Us coloured people don’t really have work. We make our living out of the sea. Now this water goes to the sea, and kills the fish. At the end of the day we have nothing to eat.

VO 17 Newly built houses around here are not even connected to the sewage pipeline - raw sewage runs straight into this stream.

VOX: We struggle here. Every day we struggle here.

VOX: We have lots of children here and they can get sick.

VO 18 What the residents of Hornlee are forced to live with is truly intolerable.

LINK The stench here is really unbearable and the sewage flowing behind me here will go through a protected wetland, via a residential area to the Ashmead channel and from there it will flow into one of the most biodiverse estuaries in the world.

VO 19 The estuary does have one saving grace and that’s the tidal exchange that flushes out some of the pollution. But, if the town’s management is not turned around, not even the tides will be able to save it.

VO 20 The community is now stepping in - like here ..this road’s repairs are being privately funded by residents.

VO 21 It’s taken years of decline to get to this point, but ward councillor Sharon Sabbagh says in recent months, it’s reached a crisis point.

UPSOUND Sharon Sabbagh / DA Ward Councillor : I would use the term that we are commercially insolvent because we do not receive enough money on a monthly basis to meet our monthly expenses.

VO 22 A ticking time bomb for both the residents and the environment. But that’s not how the Mayor sees it.

ERIN: Can you tell me, what’s the financial status of Knysna?

UPSOUND Aubrey Tsengwa: Let me be blunt because there is this notion out there that Knysna Municipality is bankrupt. We are not bankrupt at all. We do have cash flow challenges. You know and I can indicate to you to say as an Executive Mayor, I’m very proud, from the beginning of January we have appointed a new CFO.

VO 23 That’s because the two previous CFO’s or chief financial officers were unlawfully appointed, decisions that were challenged in court, and cost the Municipality more than a million rand to fight…

VO 24 ….And they lost…Wasting money from the public purse. In recent months, neighbouring municipalities have had to step in to assist with water tankers and refuse removal.

UPSOUND Sharon Sabbagh: If you look at just December in Ward 9, I had seven sewage spills into the estuary. Across there is the NSRI, there was an area there where people can swim, that was closed, no swimming allowed because of the high sewage levels of ecoli there.

CELLPHONE FOOTAGE: (COURTESY JOHN METERLERKAMP) This is Sunday morning, third of December. This is sewerage pouring into, pouring out of the sewerage pipes into this drain here, which empties into the lagoon over there. This is our Knysna Municipality.

VO 24 The acceleration of the town’s decline peaked in December.

VO 25 And, it was marred by crisis after crisis.

VO 26 This is a reservoir in Khayalethu township.

LINK The municipality pays for security at this reservoir but clearly it's not very secure. And in November of last year, a body was found in it. It along with four other reservoirs had to be drained and disinfected just before the festive season, adding to Knynsa’s water woes.

VO 27 Anyone can wander onto this site … and help themselves to water ..

VO 28 We were able to walk the circumference of this reservoir … no security stopped us to question why we were there… so…lax security, a discarded corpse…the mayor had some explaining to do.

ERIN: What happened?

UPSOUND Aubrey Tsengwa: Part of what is happening there, we’ve got security personnel which is looking after assets of this institution of the municipality. We have requested a report as to what happened, how did that particular corpse get into the dam,right, after we have received the report, we are going to process the report and take action.

VO 29 The centre of town is the business hub – it’s also where the waste depot is located – rubbish piling up, as the municipality fails to manage one of its most basic functions.

VO 30 Illegal dumping sites are now popping up across town.

UPSOUND John Meterlerkamp / Business Owner: The waste station was designed for a much smaller town. It shouldn’t be in the centre of a tourist town. The smell is incredible, the amount of rats running around is frightening.

VO 31 Businessman John Meterlerkamp says the town has grown dramatically…and has about 85,000 residents.

UPSOUND John Meterlerkamp: The last two and a half years there’s been a huge influx of people into the Western Cape. So there’s new blood coming in, there’s new businesses, there’s lots and lots of people and the infrastructure of this town has not kept pace.

VO 31 A problem, he says the municipality has ignored for years.

UPSOUND John Meterlerkamp: It doesn’t matter who it is, who rules the council. The focus has been on politics and not on the infrastructure and not on running the town. The groundswell is now to get involved. There’s this surge of anger in that things are not being done. You can write to the municipality, phone, you are ignored as a citizen.

VO 32 It’s clear there is much work to be done to save this town. Right now, that falls to the ANC led coalition.

VO 33 As sewage spills into the estuary continue to poison the home of the Knysna seahorse - the question is will politicians prioritise self-interest or will they get down to business and save the jewel of the Garden Route?

VO 34 In the meantime, its ordinary citizens who will pay the price for years of incompetent management of this municipality. …(NATSOUND “No water”) …..Their once pristine environment at the mercy of those paid to protect it.

In November last year, a decomposing body was found in one of its reservoirs. As a result, it had to be drained and disinfected, and some residents were without water for several weeks. The Knysna Local Municipality is governed by a coalition that includes the EFF, PA and PBI. It's led by the ANC. It's been plagued by governance issues since it's formation in August 2022. The rot set in long before this coalition came to power, however, but it's decline has accelerated at an alarming rate in the past year, and the town is now facing bankruptcy.
metadata.Further information: Last year, the DA spent much of the year wrapped up in litigation against the municipality for illegal appointments. Now, the DA's provincial authorities in the Western Cape have stepped in with a list of problems in a diagnostic report that will be tabled in council in March. The municipality will have to accept the report and the proposed solutions for life in the town to change. Placing the municipality under administration would be a last resort. Described as a "coalition of corruption" by the opposition (the DA), the municipality's incompetence has become visible in all quarters of this once pristine holiday town. Infrastructure MMC Beauty Charlie has allegedly done nothing to maintain infrastructure, and the collapse is visible everywhere. The buck stops with Mayor Aubrey Tshwega. What is he doing to turn the situation around? We find out.
